cards.intuition: The generator will faithfully paraphrase whatever it is shown, so unauthorized text in the context is already a breach, even if the UI hides the citation.
cards.formula: unauthorized text in context = breach already happened

cards.intuition: Apply ACLs inside the index. Post-filtering a top-k starves eligible candidates and turns result counts into an existence oracle.
cards.formula: pre-filter mandatory; post-filter starves and leaks

cards.intuition: An ACL change is a metadata update plus cache invalidation, and the lag between the decision and the last leakable copy is a security metric.
cards.formula: revocation lag = time until all derived copies die

cards.intuition: Separate clusters beat separate indexes beat namespaces beat a shared index with a filter. Know exactly which rung you operate on.
A cache keyed by query text alone hands one tenant another tenant's cached answer. Tenant and ACL context belong in every key.
cards.formula: cache key = query + tenant + ACL hash

cards.intuition: The gateway injects tenant context from the session, retrieval applies it as a mandatory filter, and the response layer re-verifies every document tag.
The payload rides the corpus, not the API: your own retriever delivers adversarial instructions at the moment of maximum relevance.
The model that reads untrusted content holds no tools and no credentials; an orchestrator acts only on its structured outputs.
cards.formula: reader cannot act; orchestrator acts on structure

cards.intuition: No complete injection defense exists, so assume success and bound its reach: a wrong answer, never a breach.
cards.formula: least privilege for the model is the real control

cards.intuition: Plant unique strings per tenant and alert if one surfaces across a boundary; they test isolation and injection delivery at once.
cards.formula: canary string in wrong answer = isolation failure
